summary: Model promote triggers cascading fallbacks during prefix-cache warmup, causing elevated latency and 5xxs
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated promote from canary -> stable for rwd-base-7b-v2 at 03/13/2026 02:40 UTC, the serving runtime returned a series of cascading fallbacks to older model variants for a portion of traffic. Root cause appears tied to prefix/KV cache warming behavior: newly promoted replicas were marked healthy and only accepted traffic before their KV cache prefixes were sufficiently populated, leading to high initial KV cache miss rates, elevated generation latencies, and a spike in internal 5xx errors from the serving runtime.

Impact:
- FoldHealth (dedicated customer) experienced ~30m of elevated median latency (token generation 2x normal) and a 6% increase in 5xx rates on their /v1/generate route.
- Some requests were routed to fallback model variants as the router enforced latency SLO-based failover, resulting in reduced output consistency for ~12% of sessions during the window.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:40:30: Canary promoted to stable via rollout automation (weight adjustments + promote).
- 02:41:00 - 03:10:00: Observed latency and 5xx spike; auto-fallbacks detected in routing logs.
- 03:12:00: Support notified by FoldHealth; incident opened.
- 03:24:00: Temporary traffic pin to previous stable applied to reduce user impact.
- 03:48:00: Rollback of the promote completed; metrics normalized by 03:55:00.

Why this is unusual:
Promotes normally rely on a warmup phase where a subset of traffic warms caches before full weight transfer. In this case the promote automation marked nodes as promotable before warmup thresholds were met because health checks focused on CPU/gpu and not KV cache fill ratio. The router's latency-based fallback logic then diverted traffic away from warmed-but-slow instances, which cascaded into more load on already warmed instances and created instability until rollback.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy rwd-base-7b-v2 variant with default promote automation in a dedicated pool.
2) Configure promote automation to mark replicas healthy on readiness probe passing (current setup checks GPU health and serving process only).
3) Simulate steady traffic at FoldHealth's 95th percentile for 5 minutes and trigger promote.
4) Observe KV cache miss rate, token generation latency, and router fallback events in the 0-30 min window after promote.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Readiness probe gating is insufficient; it doesn't measure KV cache fill ratio or prefix warm hit-rate.
Hypothesis 2: Router fallback thresholds aggressiveness caused cascading failover when a subset of instances were cold.
Checked: node readiness timestamps, KV cache metrics, router decision traces, and promote automation logs (promote_controller.log).
Found: promote_controller marked 6/8 new replicas healthy within 20s of start because service process was listening; KV prefix fill averaged 12% on those nodes at that time.
Found: router has a latency-based failover that considers 200ms p95 threshold; when a few instances exceed threshold, traffic is shifted to older variants—this amplified load on older instances.
Captured PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 (add kv_warmup_check to promote gating).
Runbook cross-check: rollout checklist currently recommends manual warmup for high-throughput dedicated customers; automation did not honor warmup flag for this pool.
resolution: Workaround applied: immediate pin to previous stable variant for FoldHealth followed by rollback of the promote. Root cause: promote automation considered instances healthy based on process-level readiness only and did not require a KV cache warmup threshold. Fixes deployed: 1) Emergency change to promote controller to include kv_prefix_fill_pct >= 70% as part of readiness gating for high-throughput pools (merged PR 4821). 2) Router fallback configuration softened for first 10 minutes after a promote so it prefers slow-but-warmed instances over immediate fallback to older variants (config change rolled out to prod-us-east at 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC). 3) Added a warmup-run in promote pipeline that issues synthetic warmup traffic to populate KV prefixes for promoted replicas before marking them fully promotable. 4) Post-incident: scheduled follow-up INT task to add observability dashboard for promote warmup metrics and update rollout runbook. Customer follow-up: Support team provided a post-incident summary and offered a synchronous review with FoldHealth engineers.
